title.en: Can Wearables and AI Predict the Next Pandemic?

source.note: No workbook sheet exists for this mission. Authored from scratch per docs/plans/new-mission-playbook.md.

stages.source_description: Part 1: Introduction (Slides 1-3: hook on a device noticing illness before you do, SDG 3's early-warning target, Taiwan's SARS/COVID data-driven track record)

title.en: An Island That Learned From SARS

stages.source_description: Part 2: Problem (Slides 4-6: symptom-based surveillance arrives late, a huge unused data stream sits on people's wrists, the critical question of whether that gap can close)
stages.language_pattern: present progressive for trends / this causes ...

title.en: A Data Stream on Every Wrist

stages.source_description: Part 3: Achievements (Slides 7-9: Taiwan CDC's AI flu-forecasting system, NTUST's one-minute wearable risk screen, the NHI Health Bank's population-scale data platform)

title.en: Half the Island, One Health Record
title.zh: 半個台灣，一本健康存摺

stages.source_description: Part 4: Solutions (Slides 10-12: feeding wearable signals into the existing surveillance pipeline, what international wearable studies already show, opt-in governance instead of mandates)

title.en: Feeding the Signal Into the System

stages.source_description: Part 5: Implications (Slides 13-16: one continuous tension — the promise of millions of early signals, the privacy barrier that promise runs into, the accuracy/noise barrier even privacy-solved data still has, and why the real question is trust, not the technology)

title.zh: 如果數百萬人選擇加入

title.en: When Noise Looks Like a Signal
The Real Question Is Not the Data
title.zh: 真正的問題不在數據本身

stages.source_description: Part 6: Call to action (Slides 17-20: what Taiwan already has, this is an engineering problem not science fiction, where STEM students fit in, closing ask)

title.en: An Engineering Problem, Not Science Fiction
title.zh: 一個工程問題，不是科幻小說
